#1833. Arsenal contract negotiations no longer a major source of stress as transformation complete

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

The international break has played out something like an Oprah Winfrey show for the Arsenal squad.

Oprah, back in 2004, marched around her studio, declaring all those in the audience had won a car. Just the 276 Pontiac G6s dished out, for those wondering.

Andrea Berta has seemingly been following that example at Arsenal. “You get a contract! You get a contract! You get a contract! You get a contract! Everybody gets a contract!”

It started with the news that Declan Rice had reached an agreement over a new long-term deal, one that will see him join Bukayo Saka on around £350,000-a-week.

Jurrien Timber, too, is set to commit his future to the club. Like Rice, he had entered the final two years of his current deal but the intention was always for Arsenal to tie him down beyond that.

There was more. David Raya has agreed fresh terms as well and will sign a new contract, a year on from receiving a pay rise. This deal will keep him at Arsenal through to 2030.

Piero Hincapie wanted in and is understood to have joined the extension club. The defender only signed for the Gunners permanently in the summer and that deal did not expire until 2031.

However, Hincapie has been rewarded with improved terms for his contribution to the title-winning season and a 12-month extension on the previous deal.

A busy period, then, for those involved in the building and managing of this squad. An extremely indicative one, too, both of how far Arsenal have come and where they want to get to.

It was not that long ago that contract negotiations for key players were a major source of stress for the club.

Under Arsene Wenger, Alexis Sanchez made it clear he had no desire to sign a new deal. Arsenal decided not to sell and he went into the last year of his contract, before joining Manchester United in a swap deal with Henrikh Mkhitaryan.

Terrified of losing Mesut Ozil for free and having been dragged into the final six months of his deal in 2018, Arsenal threw the kitchen sink at him and gave him a £350,000-a-week deal.

For years, Arsenal fans knew exactly when the contracts of the most important players would run out, almost fearing the two years leading up to that.

Premier League predictions: Standard Sport names title winners and more

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal in Vinicius talks; Man Utd deal confirmed

Arsenal get new Havertz penalty review as Premier League panel confirm error

Not so now. Rice has entered the final 18 months of his existing deal but there was no real sense of jeopardy. The assumption was always that an extension would be agreed and that has proved correct.

This is now a club that players want to sign but just as crucially want to stay at. Rice’s new deal will commit his prime years to the club, as will be the case with Raya.

You get a contract! You get a contract! You get a contract! You get a contract! Everybody gets a contract!

Had Rice wished to explore his options elsewhere, he would have had his pick of the elite clubs across Europe, as would William Saliba before he signed a new deal last year.

Arsenal might not be able to sign the most high-profile players from clubs like Real Madrid, as the summer pursuit of Vinicius Junior showed, but they can now protect their own assets regardless of who wants them.

There are still decisions to be made over other situations. Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz are both out of contract in 2028 as it stands. So too is Ben White and it is understood that as with Odegaard, no contract talks have yet taken place with the club.

However, the dynamic is very different to the one Arsenal have had to put up with in the past. These are not desperate negotiations. If these are players are leave in the transfer windows ahead, it feels like that would be a club-led decision.

These contract extensions also point to the power Mikel Arteta has and the priorities of the club. This is not about building a squad for five or six years down the line. Everything is centred towards giving Arteta the tools to win immediately.

That was apparent in the summer signings of Ezri Konsa and Bruno Guimaraes, both now 29, and in the handing out of huge contracts to take players well into their 30s.

Arteta has signed a contract of his own through to 2030 and it is all about maximising every opportunity for major trophies between now and then.

His priority is this season and the three beyond it. What happens after that, in terms of the age profile of the squad or the contract situations in the squad, might not be Arteta’s problem.

By then he might be driving off into the sunset. Probably not in a Pontiac G6.

#1832. Liverpool make surprise contract U-turn over £55m star as fresh update reveals new Reds 'talks'

By Lewis Blain | 18 Nov 2026 07:40

Liverpool have taken a significant step towards securing Alexis Mac Allister's long-term future by opening contract negotiations with the midfielder.

The Argentina international has been keen to extend his stay at Anfield, but there had been growing frustration over the lack of progress.

However, fresh claims suggest the Reds have finally changed their stance and begun discussions over a new deal.

According to reliable Argentine journalist Cesar Luis Merlo (via Sport Witness), Liverpool have opened negotiations with Mac Allister over a contract extension.

The 27-year-old's current agreement runs until June 2028, meaning the Reds have made an early move to keep him at Anfield beyond that date.

There is no agreement in place yet, and Merlo has not disclosed any proposed salary or contract length, although the coming weeks could provide a clearer indication of whether both parties can reach a compromise.

The development represents a change from the situation described by Mac Allister's father and agent, Carlos, who told ESPN Brazil just days ago that Liverpool had not started negotiations.

The long-serving star has also previously voiced his disappointment at the lack of an offer, admitting in September that he was "very, very sad" about the situation, particularly after teammates Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai had been offered new contracts.

More recently, Mac Allister attempted to reassure supporters, expressing hope that the club's board would reconsider its position.

Liverpool's reported change of heart could reflect Mac Allister's importance to Andoni Iraola's plans, with the £55m enforcer continuing to receive regular opportunities.

Starting eight of the Reds' ten Premier League matches and three of their four Champions League fixtures, he remains a prominent part of the team's midfield setup.

That level of involvement makes it difficult to justify allowing uncertainty over his future to continue, particularly when he has consistently indicated a desire to remain at Anfield.

There is still work to do before an agreement is reached, but opening discussions is an encouraging development for Liverpool.

Mac Allister has made his feelings clear, and the club now appears to be responding. Keeping an established midfielder of his importance could prove a sensible decision as Iraola continues shaping his squad.

#1831. Mauricio Pochettino at Manchester United: Will Things Finally Change at Old Trafford?

When Mauricio Pochettino walks into Anfield for his first match as Manchester United manager, he will immediately be confronted by the scale of the challenge ahead. There are easier ways to begin a reign than an away trip to Liverpool, especially for a club that has spent much of the past decade searching for stability and finding very little of it.

The symbolism is obvious. Liverpool have spent recent years building coherent teams, developing clear identities and competing regularly for major trophies, even if they did hit a few bumps on the road themselves. Manchester United have spent the same period cycling through managers, rebuilding projects and tactical resets. Pochettino’s appointment represents another attempt to break that pattern, but it would be a mistake to believe the Argentine’s task begins and ends with improving results.

His predecessors discovered that managing the team is only part of the job. The harder challenge is changing the culture and structure of a club that has repeatedly undermined its own attempts at renewal.

Pochettino was right to push back against the idea that Manchester United’s problems can be reduced to distance covered or sprint numbers.

The statistics are alarming. United have been outrun in most of their league matches and rank near the bottom of the division in several physical metrics. Yet simply demanding greater effort is unlikely to transform a struggling team overnight.

What United have lacked for years is collective purpose. Too often the team has looked like a group of talented individuals operating with different interpretations of the same game plan. When Pochettino talks about players running together and understanding their roles, he is really describing something more fundamental than fitness. He is talking about creating a collective identity.

That was one of the defining strengths of his best Tottenham side. They were physically outstanding, but their success came from organisation and belief as much as athleticism. Every player understood what was expected of him, and the team functioned as a coherent unit.

Manchester United have not consistently looked like that under any manager for a very long time.

It’s official. Mauricio is a Red 🔴📸 https://t.co/9uq47U3S3Z

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 18, 2026

The obvious counterargument is that other highly regarded coaches have arrived at Old Trafford with similarly ambitious ideas.

Erik ten Hag was respected throughout Europe. Ruben Amorim arrived with a reputation as one of the continent’s brightest tactical minds. Others before them possessed impressive credentials too.

What makes Pochettino different is the nature of his previous achievements.

Unlike some elite managers, he has rarely inherited finished products. His reputation was built on developing teams, improving players and creating environments where younger footballers could thrive. His Tottenham side became one of Europe’s best teams despite operating with fewer resources than many of their rivals, while his spell at Chelsea demonstrated an ability to stabilise a chaotic dressing room and extract improvement from a talented but unbalanced squad.

That experience feels particularly relevant at Manchester United. This is not a club requiring minor adjustments; it is a club still searching for a clear football identity. Pochettino has spent much of his career building exactly that.

Even the best coaches struggle when recruitment and management pull in different directions, and that, among other things is where Manchester United have repeatedly run into trouble.

Successive managers have inherited squads constructed for different styles of football. Players signed for one coach have remained when another arrived with entirely different ideas. The result has been an increasingly awkward collection of footballers who often appear unsuited to the system being asked of them.

If Pochettino is to succeed, that cycle cannot continue.

The club’s hierarchy must show the discipline to recruit according to a long-term strategy rather than chasing short-term fixes. That requires difficult decisions, particularly regarding players who may still carry reputations but no longer fit the demands of modern elite football.

Tottenham’s rise under Pochettino was possible because the squad gradually became an extension of the manager’s ideas. Manchester United have not reached that point under any coach since Sir Alex Ferguson.

Without alignment between the manager and recruitment department, even the strongest project stalls, and eventually fails.

Perhaps the greatest danger is expecting immediate transformation.

The temptation after years of disappointment will be to judge Pochettino’s reign through the lens of short-term results. That is understandable, especially when the club sits far below the standards many expect from them.

Yet rebuilding rarely follows a straight line. Pochettino’s first Tottenham team finished fifth before progressing into genuine title challengers, and Champions League finalists. Many of the players who later became stars required time and patience. The same principle is likely to apply at Old Trafford.

His opening fixture at Liverpool serves as a reminder of how much work remains to be done. Whatever happens at Anfield, it should not define the project. The more important question is whether United begin to look like a team with direction.

For all the doom that surrounds Manchester United, the club remains one of football’s great institutions. The fanbase remains enormous, the resources remain substantial, and the attraction of the badge has not disappeared yet.

Pochettino himself acknowledged that reality when discussing the scale of the support he encounters around the world. That is why the job continues to draw elite managerial candidates despite the obvious risks. The potential rewards remain extraordinary. The challenge is converting potential into reality.

The honest answer is yes, but only under conditions that have often been absent at Manchester United.

Pochettino has the coaching pedigree. He has the experience of handling demanding environments. He has a proven track record of improving players and building teams. Whether that is enough depends largely on whether the club has learned from the mistakes that consumed previous managers.

If United continue changing direction every couple of years, no coach will succeed. If they provide Pochettino with time, authority and recruitment aligned to a coherent football vision, then he may have a better chance than most of restoring the club to relevance at the top of the Premier League.

His first game – away to Liverpool – is obviously a daunting introduction to the task ahead. In many ways, it will be a good indicator of where Manchester United currently stand. They are beginning another chapter while measuring themselves against a rival that has spent years getting the fundamentals right.

Pochettino’s challenge is not simply to win matches. It is to ensure that, a few years from now, Manchester United are finally discussing how to compete for titles again rather than debating the future of yet another manager.

Liverpool have received a surprise boost ahead of their Premier League showdown against Manchester United, with star striker Alexander Isak handed a rest while on international duty.

Sweden boss Graham Potter pledged to name a strong team against Poland for the Nations League B dead rubber - the Swedes already confirmed as group winners ahead of kick-off.

But despite that promise, Isak remained on the bench for the full 90 minutes on Tuesday night as Sweden secured a 1-1 draw in Poland to conclude a successful Nations League campaign.

Sweden will move up to the top tier of the Nations League for the 2028-29 edition of the competition, allowing Isak to mix with Europe’s elite on the international stage.

Isak missed three games for Sweden during the last international break after picking up a thigh issue, which then prevented the 27-year-old from featuring for Liverpool against Manchester City and LASK.

But rather than returning from international duty with an injury, this time Isak will come back to Merseyside fully rested for Sunday’s clash with Man United.

So far this season, Isak has made 14 appearances for Liverpool across all competitions, grabbing eight goals and one assist.

After an injury-frustrated debut season at Anfield - Isak suffering a fibula fracture in December - following his £130million move from Newcastle, the Swede has become a central figure to Andoni Iraola’s plans.

Aside from the two games he missed due to a thigh issue, Isak has played minutes in every fixture he has been available for.

Isak has only faced Man Utd once as a Liverpool player, taken off after 72 minutes at Anfield during a 2-1 defeat in October 2025 before missing the return fixture at Old Trafford due to an adductor issue.

After a poor start to the season, United sit 18th in the Premier League with just one win in 10 games and are out of the Carabao Cup after a defeat at home to Brighton in September.

United’s players have been booed by supporters at Old Trafford but Neville believes Diogo Dalot has been made an ‘easy target’ and has defended the Portuguese full-back because of his work-rate.

Neville also feels Pochettino will look to move on Noussair Mazraoui, Matthijs de Ligt, Mason Mount, Marcus Rashford and Joshua Zirkzee at the end of the campaign, and expects Lisandro Martinez to leave when his contract expires next summer.

‘Do I think Dalot is Denis Irwin? No. Let’s be really clear, Denis Irwin is the greatest full-back Manchester United have ever had, I shouldn’t be mentioning him in the same breath, but I would get rid of a few before Dalot,’ Neville said on Stick to United.

‘I’d be getting rid of Mazraoui well before him. I’d be getting rid of Martinez well before him. I’d be getting rid of De Ligt well before him.

‘He’ll work with Amad, he’ll work with Mbeumo, he’ll work with Cunha and he’ll work with Sesko and think, ‘okay, I’ll make you into a centre-forward’.

‘And then the year after you’d be looking at Shaw, Maguire, Dalot, Bruno, that’s your second wave and maybe then you’ve made your mind up on Baleba and Santos.

‘But the earliest Mauricio Pochettino can unravel this squad is two seasons if he does well. It could take three to get this squad unravelled.’

#1823. England’s potential path to glory proves Nations League is more difficult to win than the World Cup

Sometimes you have to say the unsayable because no one else will.

The Nations League is a more difficult competition to win than the World Cup or the European Championships. Stay with me.

Though there remain plenty of club football fans who take no interest in international football outside of major tournaments and are sceptical about the Nations League, there has been a noticeable drop in the number of club fans repeating the trite notion it is a pointless competition made up of glorified friendlies no one cares about.

My hunch as to why: people are beginning to realise how much of a refreshing addition to the football it really is, plus how many tasty fixtures it produces. And it is that final point — the competition regularly throwing up blockbuster clashes between European heavyweights — that explains why the Nations League might just be the hardest competition to win in international football.

A disclaimer is needed at this point. The Nations League is not a major tournament like the World Cup or European Championships are. Those competitions take place in single block international breaks during the summer (except when hosted in the Middle East) and the stakes at play mean immeasurably more pressure and psychological challenges as players and teams seek to win the trophies that matter most.

The World Cup and Euros remain more psychologically draining and patently more important. But more difficult to win than the Nations League in a footballing sense? Honestly, no.

The calibre of opposition is far higher in Europe’s newest event compared with the World Cup or Euros. Just look at Argentina’s route to the World Cup final where they were defeated by Spain.

They faced Algeria, Austria, debutants Jordan, fellow debutants Cape Verde, Egypt, Switzerland and then finally one world-football powerhouse, England, and were suddenly into a World Cup final.

For all their memories of their best World Cup finish since 1966, England’s route to their semi-final defeat to Argentina was not much more difficult. Croatia, Ghana, Panama, DR Congo, Mexico, and finally Norway.

And in their previous tournament, when England limped to the Euro 2024 final under Gareth Southgate with a string of uninspiring performances, they faced Serbia, Denmark, Slovenia, Slovakia, Switzerland and the Netherlands — and navigating that pretty presentable route meant they had qualified for the final and a shot at becoming European champions.

And what made this summer’s expanded World Cup even less likely to produce those big fixtures was FIFA’s brazenly cynical introduction of Wimbledon-styled protected ranking at its seeding stage.

The world’s four top-ranked nations would be kept apart in different quarters of the draw until the semi-finals providing they each won their groups. Shock: they all did.

Sure enough, for the first time in history the four top ranks made up the men’s World Cup semi-finalists: Argentina, England, France and Spain. A great product, just as FIFA wanted, but it had taken 100 matches to get there, the only blockbuster fixture among 72 group matches having been Spain and Uruguay, two former winners.

Winter energy bill misery on way as price cap set to jump by 26% in January

England’s Ivan Toney fails in bid to move assault trial over Euro 2028 clash

Nations League draw simulated as England get favourable quarter-final tie

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

The World Cup was great, but plenty of its matches had been rather too easy to call beforehand.

The calibre of opposition is far higher in Europe’s newest event compared with the World Cup or Euros

Now consider England’s potential path to Nations League glory next summer. A group stage first of all where England faced Czechia, Croatia and world champions Spain home and away.

Croatia are a good footballing nation but by finishing third of the group are now out, with next March to bring together only the winners and runners up from the four groups for the quarter-finals.

Group A3 winners England will face either Belgium, the Netherlands or Erling Haaland’s Norway — the teams ranked eighth, ninth and 19th in the world rankings.

After a two-legged tie against one of those opponents, England would gear up for next summer’s Nations League Finals, a one-off semi-final and then potentially a final, with France, Germany or Portugal as their likeliest opponents in those two games.

Here is a string of prestige fixtures far more testing for Thomas Tuchel’s side than the World Cup produced. No comparison in pressure and scrutiny, granted, but tougher in purely footballing terms, undoubtedly — and coaches are not rotating their teams or resting players as much as one might imagine. It is taken seriously.

For its sheer hit rate of big games out of the total set of fixtures and for how consistently well a top team would have to perform to navigate them all, the UEFA Nations League has become international football’s most difficult competition to win. There. Sometimes you have to say the unsayable because no one else will.

Waddle’s comments come amid mounting speculation over Scott’s future, with Bournemouth bracing themselves for incoming offers to steal their prized possession away in the January transfer window.

Scott’s eye-catching breakthrough in the international arena has done little to quieten rumours that the 23-year-old could soon be destined for bigger and better things, with Chelsea, Arsenal, Manchester City and Tottenham all rumoured to be circling.

In an interview with iGaming.com, ex-England international Waddle revealed how he had been keeping close tabs on Scott’s progress since he was first alerted to his potential at Bristol City.

‘I’ve always liked Alex Scott. I think he’s a lovely, cultured player. There’s no doubt in my mind that in the last eighteen months, the kid’s taken his game to a new level,’ Waddle explained.

‘I followed him at Bristol City, and when he was there, I was speaking to someone that knew him who told me he was a Tottenham fan.

However, Waddle insists Scott should ideally be aiming higher than a move to Stamford Bridge, name-checking Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal as potential options.

While Bournemouth are in no hurry to part with Scott, the club’s hierarchy recognise that the England international may have ambitions to move on elsewhere near future.

For now, though, the Cherries are adamant that the Vitality Stadium remains the ‘right place’ for Scott.

By Darren Plant | 18 Nov 2026 09:30

Not only does Caicedo now face a long-haul flight from Ecuador, he is giving up five hours of recovery due to the time difference between Guayaquil and London.

Jordan Henderson was not called up by England, whereas Romeo Lavia played on Sunday night having missed Belgium's first of two UEFA Nations game during the international break.

#1820. Why Manchester United kit selection vs Liverpool could be a good omen - with one glaring exception

Mauricio Pochettino has potentially been handed a positive omen for his first game in charge of Manchester United.

The Argentine begins his tenure as Red Devils boss with the daunting prospect of facing the club’s biggest rivals away from home, with the two sides in contrasting form.

Pochettino arrives at a club currently in the bottom three of the Premier League, while Andoni Iraola has Liverpool fourth in the Premier League table after 10 games.

For Sunday’s trip to Anfield, Man United have confirmed they will wear this season’s third kit which consists of white shirts and black shorts.

Interestingly, Man Utd’s four most recent victories at the home of their arch rivals have come with the players wearing white shirts, including the away half of last season’s double.

Harry Maguire’s header late on gave Man United a 2-1 win at Anfield, ending a run of 10 games without a win for Man United at Anfield.

To find further wins in white for Manchester United at Anfield you would have to go back to Louis van Gaal’s reign.

In 2016 Wayne Rooney’s strike sealed a smash-and-grab 1-0 win against Jurgen Klopp’s Liverpool, with Juan Mata starring the year prior.

However, fans will recall that Man United wore white when they were embarrassed 7-0 at Anfield in March 2023.

Coincidentally, Man Utd are undefeated at Anfield since that humbling loss, picking up two draws and a win in their last three visits to Liverpool. On those occasions Man Utd wore all white.

There was a large gap between white strips for Manchester United on trips to Anfield, with a six-year wait between a 2-0 defeat in the Europa League in 2016 and a 4-0 hammering in 2022.

And while Nyoni was taken off before the hour-mark on Merseyside, it’s clear Odegaard left a big impression on the 19-year-old in the 58 minutes his opposite number was on the pitch.

Asked to name the ‘toughest’ player he has come up against, Nyoni told The Inside Scoop, ‘For me personally, I would say Odegaard,’ as he looked back on that afternoon.

When asked if Odegaard perhaps doesn’t get the credit he deserves, Nyoni replied: ‘Yeah, I think the game is evolving and I think nowadays people look at No.10s and automatically think that if they’re not getting goals and assists, they’re not good.

‘For example, in our team we’ve got Flo [Wirtz]. I think Flo does a lot of stuff that people don’t really see.

‘I think what he brings to the team benefits the team. Just because he’s not scoring or assisting, doesn’t mean he’s not effective.

‘Nowadays, the idea that if a player isn’t getting goals or assists, they’re useless, but every player has their own role in the team.

‘Odegaard and people like Flo, if they’re not getting goals and assists, people that don’t watch the game automatically think they haven’t played well but that’s not how football works.’

In the aftermath of Arsenal’s nervy win over Hull, club legend Paul Merson said Odegaard had been ‘like a new signing’ for Arteta this season.

‘He’s been outstanding. He’s the only one really that moves it quickly,’ Merson said of Odegaard on Sky Sports.

#1814. Chelsea injury news: Xabi Alonso in double boost ahead of Leeds United showdown

By Darren Plant | 18 Nov 2026 09:58

Chelsea have been handed a double injury boost ahead after Emiliano Martinez and Aaron Anselmino both represented Argentina on Tuesday night.

Martinez and Anselmino were called up by Lionel Scaloni despite spending weeks and months on the sidelines.

While goalkeeper Martinez had been unavailable with a fractured jaw since October 17, Anselmino has not played any competitive minutes for Chelsea in 2026-27 due to a hamstring injury.

However, the pair featured as Argentina cruised to a 7-0 victory over Costa Rica in Cordoba.

Starting between the sticks wearing a protective mask, Martinez played the full 90 minutes, albeit only having to make two saves during a one-sided contest.

Meanwhile, Anselmino was introduced as a 71st-minute substitute as the former world champions saw out the win.

Anselmino's outing - his first for Argentina - is particularly notable because it is his first since a 29-minute appearance in a pre-season friendly versus Johor DT on August 9.

When Moises Caicedo has provided a further fitness concern for Xabi Alonso, having Martinez and Anselmino come through unscathed for Argentina is a welcome boost.

Alonso must now decide whether to retain Mike Penders for Saturday's Premier League game with Leeds United or hand an immediate recall to Martinez.

Given the time difference and Penders having largely impressed in his absence, Martinez may expect to be named on the substitutes' bench.

Although it is possible that Anselmino will not feature in Chelsea's squad versus Leeds, Alonso requires an extra central-defensive option due to Maxence Lacroix being expected to be sidelined until January.

Realistically, the 21-year-old could be handed a start for the Blues' Under-21s ranks before coming into contention for the first team.

#1813. Manchester United confirm FIVE departures as Mauricio Pochettino overhaul begins

Manchester United have confirmed the departures of five members of staff after Mauricio Pochettino began work as the club’s new manager on Wednesday.

The Argentine was pictured arriving at Carrington for his first day in charge of the Red Devils, having flown immediately over after his final match with the United States.

The 54-year-old oversaw the USMNT’s 2-0 victory over Haiti in Cincinnati on Tuesday before getting a flight straight over to Manchester with his long-serving assistant manager Miguel D’Agostino, who will join him at Old Trafford.

His other backroom staff have already been confirmed by United, with Toni Jimenez, Jesus Perez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino, his son, all joining him in the north west.

The aforementioned quartet departed the US early for Old Trafford - before Tuesday’s match with Haiti - to begin work early ahead of Pochettino’s first game in charge.

He takes his new side to Anfield to face Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool on Sunday.

It does mean that the coaches that assisted Michael Carrick, Pochettino’s predecessor, have left the club, with United confirming as much on their website on Wednesday.

Jonathan Woodgate, Steve Holland, Travis Binnion, Craig Mawson and Jonny Evans were all part of the now-sacked head coach’s support crew, but it was clear that their jobs were in danger after the former midfielder’s sacking last Thursday.

Evans, the ex-United defender, was photographed leaving Carrington in his car on Thursday morning with boxes piled up behind him as he drove away, with many speculating that he had served his final day at his former club.

#1811. Ex-Manchester United star calls for ‘change at the top’ amid Mauricio Pochettino verdict

Ashley Young believes Manchester United will continue to struggle until the club changes the way it is run, while he is also unsure whether Mauricio Pochettino will have enough time to implement his ideas.

United announced the appointment of Pochettino on a two-and-a-half-year deal to succeed Michael Carrick this week, with the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss set to take his first training session on Thursday.

Pochettino becomes the fourth permanent manager to take the reins at Old Trafford since INEOS and Sir Jim Ratcliffe bought a minority stake and took over the day-to-day running of United in February 2024.

Upon buying a 27.5 per cent stake in the club, Ratcliffe insisted United needed to put a stop to the managerial turnover that had become commonplace since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement in 2013.

Yet just over two-and-a-half years on, nothing has changed, with Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Carrick all being shown the door.

Pochettino has a huge task on his hands, with United currently sitting in the relegation zone, and Young believes that even if results initially improve, significant change won’t occur until changes are made in the boardroom.

“This season has been tough. I've said that Michael Carrick worked miracles last season with the squad that was there,” Young tells Standard Sport.

“Do I think things still need to change? Yeah, I think until things change from the top down to the manager, (United will continue to struggle). I think that things might start well, but there's always going to be some issues there.”

Pochettino has been on United’s radar for several years, and he came close to taking the head coach role on a number of occasions over the last decade before eventually agreeing to take over from Carrick.

Revered for his time in charge of Tottenham between 2014 and 2019, Pochettino has since struggled to replicate the same success he enjoyed in north London, and he leaves the US men’s national team having met rather than exceeded expectations at the World Cup this summer.

United will be aware they are not appointing the same Pochettino they courted in 2016, when the Argentine was heavily linked with the role after Louis van Gaal’s departure, and have therefore handed him a short-term deal.

This season has been tough. I've said that Michael Carrick worked miracles last season with the squad that was there

Young, though, is not sure whether Pochettino will have enough time to instil his ideas and stabilise the club after a disastrous start to the season.

“I think Mauricio Pochettino has probably gone in and said that he wants reassurances that he's going to get the players in and get the players out that he needs,” Young continued.

“But if you look at, especially when he was at Tottenham, it took him two or three years to rebuild that side. He got players in that were hungry, that wanted to play for him.

“I think if you talk to players that have played for him, it's going to be tough, it's going to be hard. So I think there's going to be a rebuild there.

“But also, he's been given a two-and-a-half-year contract. At Tottenham, it was three years to rebuild the team.

“So I think that's interesting in itself. Hopefully things can go better and go well, and the club can be stabilised. But I still think that something needs to change at the top.”

Young was speaking ahead of the launch of the Panini Official EFL Sticker Collection and said his first memories of collecting the stickers came as a kid at school.

“I always said that, you know, when you used to open packs and get a shiny (sticker), it was the best feeling ever. It was like Christmas come all over again.

“First memories of swapping at school as well. Kids at break time were like, ‘have you got this, have you got that?’ Trying to get the best ones.”

#1808. Man United transfer news: Major new rival emerges in race for Alejandro Balde

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 10:15

Lacking game time at Barcelona, Alejandro Balde is looking for a way out in January, with Paris Saint-Germain only just appearing in the picture.

Alejandro Balde is set to be one of the talking points of the winter transfer window. Struggling at Barcelona, where his game time has fallen considerably, the 23-year-old left-back is considering leaving to find a bigger role elsewhere.

His record this season is particularly meagre, with five appearances and only 124 minutes played. It is a situation that contrasts sharply with the status the Spaniard enjoyed in Catalonia until very recently.

According to the latest information from Spain and Italy, several clubs are following his situation. Juventus are considering a loan, while Monaco are eyeing a bigger move. Now Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United have also entered the fray.

Manchester United are reportedly going all out to sign Balde in January.

According to TEAMtalk, the club’s recruitment department believes the left-back has a high ceiling and Barcelona are open to a loan, which would allow Manchester United to assess him before committing to a permanent deal.

The same report says Balde is willing to move to the Premier League and that his relationship with Barcelona manager Hansi Flick is ‘completely broken and glacial’.

Fabrizio Romano has described the chance of a January exit as ‘serious and concrete’, adding that Balde is ‘genuinely ready to consider leaving’ and exploring options with his agent, Jorge Mendes. Manchester United were interested in the summer but did not proceed, with Balde considered too expensive for a left-back, in talks said to have involved a fee of €50m-€55m (£42.5m-£46.5m) and a net salary of more than €5m (£4.3m).

Valued at around €40m (£34m), the Barcelona player represents a market opportunity for Paris Saint-Germain. At 23, Balde already has significant experience at the highest level and still has room for improvement.

Quick and explosive, he fits the profile of a modern full-back and offers better guarantees than Lucas Digne, the disappointing summer signing. His ability to get in behind and create overloads would give Luis Enrique’s team another attacking dimension, and the move could also be a fresh start for a player who has lost confidence and continuity at Barcelona, not least because Luis Enrique rotates his starting line-up heavily.

The main obstacle is Nuno Mendes, who owns the left-back position at Paris Saint-Germain and is one of the best players in the world in that role, if not the best.

At 24, the Portuguese is a major part of the club’s project, and the left-footed Balde cannot play on the right side of defence, unless the manager comes up with something.

Luis Enrique also generally prefers a right-footed winger on the left, so Paris Saint-Germain could sign an excellent player without offering him a lasting prospect of starting, with a real risk of frustration.

#1803. Manchester United identify three Premier League signings for Mauricio Pochettino in January transfer window

Pochettino arrived at United’s training ground on Wednesday afternoon to begin his stint as head coach following the decision to sack Michael Carrick last week.

United have faced criticism over their transfer activity in the summer as they spent £155 million on signing three midfielders in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba.

Pochettino now arrives at Old Trafford short of options with striker Benjamin Sesko sidelined until next year with a shin injury, while Luke Shaw has missed United’s last seven fixtures.

According to Sky Sports, United are willing to bolster Pochettino’s squad in the January window and the club will consult the Argentine over any potential signings.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The report claims that Everton centre-back Jarrad Branthwaite and Fulham’s Calvin Bassey are two players who United are considering for January.

United had two bids rejected for Branthwaite in 2024, including an offer of £50 million, and held talks with the defender’s representatives earlier this year.

The report adds that Fulham left-back Antonee Robinson is also one of United’s options and the 29-year-old has already played under Pochettino with the United States national team.

Elsewhere, reports in Spain claim that Barcelona left-back Alejandro Balde is open to a move to United in the upcoming transfer window.

United had considered a deal for Balde in the summer but the 23-year-old wanted to fight for his place at Barca.

However, Balde has not started a game in La Liga or the Champions League this season and Barcelona remain open to selling the defender.

#1802. Manchester United make January transfer decision as Mauricio Pochettino ‘identifies targets’

Manchester United are set to back Mauricio Pochettino the January transfer window.

Sky Sports reports that the Red Devils are prepared to sanction some signings for their new manager in the winter, with the club currently sat in the Premier League relegation zone.

Pochettino, who arrived at Carrington to begin work on Wednesday, will be tasked with guiding United away from the bottom three and as high up the top-flight table as he can, while also seeing how far he can get his new side in the Champions League.

The 54-year-old will be keen to stamp his authority on the playing squad at Old Trafford, particularly with a number of key players’ contracts expiring at the end of the current campaign.

Bruno Fernandes, Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw will also see their deals come to an end in the north west in the summer, and there has not yet been much movement in regards to extensions for any of the quartet.

Captain Fernandes turned down a second new contract offer last week to throw his future further into doubt, while question marks remain over the other three.

It is believed that United are eyeing reinforcements at centre-back, left-back and up front in the upcoming transfer window, with injuries hampering them across all three positions.

At left-back and centre-forward, they are particularly light after issues for Shaw, Patrick Dorgu and Benjamin Sesko.

Pochettino is expected to be consulted on any potential incomings at Old Trafford, and it is thought that the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss will have significant input into who comes through the door.

#1800. Moises Caicedo reveals why he asked to come off for Ecuador in latest Chelsea scare

Moises Caicedo has revealed he asked to be substituted at half-time playing for Ecuador as Chelsea were handed a scare during the international break.

Ecuador played friendly matches against Costa Rica and Bolivia, picking up 2-0 victories in both games.

Caicedo played 84 minutes in Quito in what was Marcelo Gallardo’s first game in charge on Saturday, named in the starting XI again on Tuesday.

The former Brighton star was replaced halfway through that game, later revealing he was ‘not feeling well’ with Chelsea’s game against Leeds United on Saturday in his thoughts.

‘No, I didn’t feel very well, so I asked to come off instead, because I know I have another commitment with my club.,’ Caicedo told reporters. ‘So, I’ll try to get there as soon as possible and recover.’

He was ruled out of the next three games but has started Chelsea’s last five in the Premier League.

He was also a doubt heading into the game against Sunderland before the international break.

During the international break, the 25-year-old opened up on his recent fitness issues.

#1799. Ex-Chelsea chief accepts new role at former Premier League champions

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea’s former techincal director Michael Emenalo has taken up an advisory role at Leicester City.

The Athletic reports that the Nigerian, who was with the Blues for five and a half years, is part of a team of consultants that is helping the Foxes with their future planning.

The fallen giants are now in League One after back-to-back relegations from the Premier League and the Championship, and the 2016 top-flight champions currently sit 11th in the third tier.

Russell Martin, the ex-Southampton and Rangers manager, is the man tasked with taking the east Midlands side back into the second division, but financial restraints have hindered their progress.

Now, they have turned to Emenalo and his team of Deloitte consultants to help them strategise for the coming months.

Emenalo, who was a left-back in his playing days, was most recently the ‘chief football executive’ for the entire Saudi Pro League, taking up the position in July 2023.

He departed in the summer of 2026 after three years in the post, where he headed up the ‘Player Acquisition Center of Excellence’ programme.

It was his job to help draw high-profile players to the Middle East in a bid to expand the league’s popularity.

The former Nigeria interrnational now makes a return to England to assist Leicester, but it is believed that Deloitte’s task does not extend to helping plan for the sale of the club.

The 2021 FA Cup winners’ owners, the Srivaddhanaprabha family, sought the expertise of Citibank to help them with a prospective sale, putting together a brochure to showcase the club’s assets to send on to investors.

The Foxes were reportedly valued at £200million, although no interested party is thought to have met that figure.

#1797. Mauricio Pochettino reveals what he will ‘bring’ in first message to Manchester United fans

Mauricio Pochettino has listed the three things he is hoping to bring to Manchester United in his first message to fans.

The Argentine arrived at his new club on Wednesday, touching down in Manchester immediately after overseeing his final game in charge of the United States.

He led the USMNT to a 2-0 victory over Haiti on Tuesday in Cincinnati, before boarding a flight to England with his trusted assistant Miguel D’Agostino, who will work with him at Old Trafford.

The 54-year-old began work at Carrington on Wednesday, meeting with the players and club hierarchy, as he was pictured with director of football Omar Berrada.

In his first message to United fans, posted to the club’s social media channels, he said: “I am looking forward to meeting you guys.

“I have heard so many good things about you. I hope we bring all the happiness, working together and connect[ion], so that it is going to be a special season, and to make our players fight on the field and get the results we deserve.”

Pochettino’s first game in charge of United will be a tricky one, as he takes his new side to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday.

He finds the Red Devils mired in the Premier League relegation zone after just one win in 11 matches, a run that saw his predecessor Michael Carrick sacked last Thursday.

Pochettino has plenty of Premier League experience in his managerial career, having overseen Southampton, Totttenham and Chelsea before spells at Paris Saint-Germain and in the United States.

#1796. Chelsea: Mykhailo Mudryk points finger for drugs ban as Tottenham loan star prepares for comeback

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Mykhailo Mudryk has blamed the Ukrainian football association for his doping ban.

The Chelsea winger, currently on loan at Tottenham, sat out the entirety of the 2025-26 season due to a positive drugs test for meldonium, a banned substance, back in October 2024.

The substance is believed to enhance stamina and respiratory capacity.

The forward was allowed to play once more in the summer, when his four-year ban, that he appealed through the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), was lifted.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso pushed for the winger to go out on loan to earn regular game time, and he reunited with his former boss at Shakhtar Donetsk, Roberto De Zerbi, at Spurs.

Now, Mudryk has pointed the finger at the Ukrainian FA for the ‘adverse finding’ in his out-of-competition sample that was supplied two years ago.

"It was a bolt from the blue,” he said of his positive drugs test on Ukrainian podcast ‘Guest of Gordon’.

“I couldn’t believe it was true. It was like falling off a skyscraper. In a dream you would hit the ground. In life, I just kept on failing. It hit me very hard, mentally.”

The 25-year-old claims that he had never heard of meldonium, insisting that there was “no security” on international duty.

“It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe,” he explained. “It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England.”

Asked how it had got into his system, he replied: "The Ukrainian national team has absolutely no security system. At clubs, when you travel to an away game, there are always people responsible for what happens on the hotel floors and in the team.

“There are people who keep an eye on it. In the Ukrainian national team we have a nutritionist who hands us pills every couple of days before games.

“He brings us a little cup. Everyone has to take the pills that are in that cup.”

The winger, who moved to Stamford Bridge in 2023 for an initial £62million - that could rise to £89m - was asked point-blank if he blamed his national setup.

He is hoped to be back this weekend for Spurs’ home game against Ipswich.

#1794. Onana pens new Aston Villa deal: It’s been amazing so far

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Amadou Onana is relishing the opportunity to extend his stay at Aston Villa after he signed a new deal with Unai Emery's team.

Onana joined Villa from Everton for a reported £50m in 2024, and has made 72 appearances for the Villans, scoring seven goals.

However, the 25-year-old is out for the majority of this campaign after he sustained a cruciate ligament injury.

Yet that has not stopped Villa from offering the Belgium international fresh terms, and he is thrilled to stay on.

"Everyone at this football club just made me feel so welcome, from the first day – the staff, the players," Onana said.

"The fans, I obviously have a very special connection with them as well, so it means a lot for me to be able to renew my contract.

"[Unai is] very important – he's the main man. If we are in this position, this situation we are in, it's thanks to him.

"He's done incredible things at this football club, four years in a row in Europe, winning a Europa League in the third year, I think that's something very special and we all have to thank him for that.

"If I'm renewing and re-signing a new deal, I must be enjoying it! It's been amazing so far. They've definitely improved me as a player and made me a better player, so I'm grateful to them, but there's still a lot of work to do.

"It's a big one for me, for the club to take the initiative to renew my contract while I'm recovering from such a big injury, it means a lot.

"It's definitely made me a lot stronger, and I learned a lot about myself as well. Sometimes it gets dark, and that's when you need those people around you – people from here, the staff – but I'm very grateful for how it's going so far. I can't wait to be back."

Paul Ince still cannot wrap his head around Manchester United’s decision to spend £50million on Andrey Santos in the summer transfer window.

Santos completed a £50m move from Chelsea over the summer, arriving alongside Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba as the Red Devils sought to bolster their depth in central midfield.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Mykhailo Mudryk has revealed that Xabi Alonso personally persuaded him to leave Chelsea on loan.

The Ukrainian, who returned from a drugs ban for meldonium in the summer, joined Tottenham in a Deadline Day switch that saw him reunite with his former manager Roberto De Zerbi, who coached him at Skakhtar Donetsk.

The winger was the subject of much Premier League interest when it came apparent that he was available for a temporary move, and he revealed on Ukrainian podcast ‘Guest of Gordon’ that Brighton, Brentford and Leeds all registered their interest in him.

He is expected to return to action this weekend when the north Londoners take on newly-promoted Ipswich Town at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, coming off the back of a run of three wins in their last four games.

Spurs’ recent resurgence was dealt an abrupt end by Leeds at Elland Road before the recent international break, with a Noah Okafor goal on 79 minutes the difference in Yorkshire to snap De Zerbi’s three-game winning streak.

#1791. Max Dowman breaks Jude Bellingham record: what makes the Arsenal gem so special?

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 11:31

Max Dowman, who turns 17 soon, has already made history in the Premier League, the Champions League and for England

It seems that every piece of news about Max Dowman starts the same way: the young Arsenal player has broken another record. At 16, the Englishman has already been the youngest player to score in the Premier League, to play in the Champions League and to win the English league title.

This week, he added two more marks to the list: he became the youngest player to represent the England Under-21s and, three days later, the youngest to score for the side, surpassing records that belonged to Jude Bellingham.

The question is not only how many more records he can break, but what makes Dowman such a special talent and how far his characteristics can take him. The combination of individual skill, ball carrying, strength to compete physically and understanding of the game helps to explain why he can already produce against much older opponents.

Dowman was born on 31 December 2009 and joined Arsenal as a child. His progress through the youth ranks was so rapid that, at 13, he was already playing for the Under-18s. In September 2024, aged 14 years and eight months, he made his debut in the UEFA Youth League, an Under-19 competition, and became the youngest scorer in the history of the tournament.

The midfielder began training with the first team at 14 and took part in the 2025 pre-season. In August of that year, aged 15 years and 235 days, he made his Premier League debut against Leeds United. He was the second-youngest player to appear in the competition’s history, behind only Ethan Nwaneri, his Arsenal team-mate.

In November 2025, an even more significant milestone arrived. Coming on in the 3-0 win over Slavia Prague in the Champions League, Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the tournament’s history, aged 15 years and 308 days. He was also the first 15-year-old to play in the competition.

The 2025-26 season brought two more high-profile records. In March, he scored against Everton and, aged 16 years and 73 days, became the youngest scorer in Premier League history, beating James Vaughan’s mark by 197 days.

Months later, he went down in Arsenal history as the youngest player to win the Premier League. The medal came at 16 years and 144 days, when the club ended a 22-year wait for the title. In October, he received three Guinness World Records certificates for the achievements.

Now, the England Under-21s have added two more chapters. Dowman made his debut for the side against Portugal on 13 November, aged 16 years and 317 days, surpassing Bellingham’s mark as the youngest player to represent the age group. On the following Monday, he started for the first time and scored the winning goal against France, aged 16 years and 320 days. Bellingham had scored his first Under-21 goal aged 17 years and 67 days.

Records broken for Arsenal and England (born 31/12/2009)

If he scores for the senior England team before 12/11/2027, Dowman will surpass Wayne Rooney (17 years and 317 days, in 2003) as the youngest scorer for England.

Age in years (y) and days (d) on the date of each record. n/a = previous holder not confirmed by an official source. Data up to 17/11/2026.

Sources: Arsenal, Premier League, ESPN and TNT Sports

Dowman’s main characteristic is his ability to carry the ball and beat opponents. He finds it easy to receive under pressure, shield possession with his body and change direction in tight spaces. He does not rely on straight-line speed alone: he uses feints, changes of pace and short movements to unbalance defenders.

Dowman already had a physique that allowed him to compete with older players, but he has also developed an intelligent way of using his body to protect the ball. That explains why he does not seem so intimidated when facing professional defenders.

Left-footed, he usually plays on the right, from where he can cut inside and use his dominant foot. The position also allows him to receive wide, draw the opposing full-back and choose between accelerating towards the box, combining with a team-mate or finding a pass inside. His ball control and ability to change the direction of play make him a particularly difficult threat to handle one-on-one.

But reducing him to a dribbling winger would ignore an important part of his repertoire. Dowman also has experience playing as an attacking midfielder and in deeper roles. In the youth ranks, he even played as a deep-lying midfielder. This variety helped him develop a broader understanding of space and the different roles on the pitch.

That versatility is an advantage for Arteta. At Arsenal, Dowman has already been used on the right and in central positions. When he receives between the lines, he can turn quickly and carry the ball towards the opposition defence. If he starts wide, he can attack the space between full-back and centre-back, moving closer to the box to shoot or take part in a combination.

There are also signs that his play without the ball matches his technical quality. In the win over France, Lee Carsley highlighted the teenager’s defensive performance, as he dropped back to intercept a pass and joined the pressing of opponents. A willingness to recover, press and take part in collective actions is an important requirement for earning a place in a side like Arteta’s.

Dowman’s rise inevitably prompts comparisons. His path recalls, in some respects, that of Nwaneri, who also made his Arsenal debut very young and had to find space in a competitive squad. Both came through the youth ranks playing in central positions, but had their first opportunities in the first team on the right.

The difference is that Dowman seems to have an even clearer ability to carry the ball at speed and beat opponents one-on-one. That does not mean it is possible to determine who will have the more successful career.

Arsenal also have reason to manage expectations. The recent episode against Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup highlighted one area of concern. After suffering a heavy challenge, the teenager reacted and was sent off, receiving a three-match ban. Arteta criticised the player publicly and said professional football is not an environment protected from provocation and the consequences of one’s own actions.

There is also the question of workload. A player who starts playing professional matches so early needs physical and emotional support. Arsenal have recent experience of integrating young players such as Saka, Nwaneri and Lewis-Skelly, but each athlete has his own process.

His first professional contract will be signed when he turns 17 on 31 December, after he agreed a pre-contract with Arsenal in January. The decision to stay at the club is important for the continuity of a development that has been closely monitored since the youth ranks.

The path to the senior England team is also open, but does not need to be taken immediately. Bellingham, who lost the Under-21 records to Dowman, played only four matches at that level before being promoted to the senior team.

For now, the best way to assess Dowman is to look at what he can already do, without turning every record into a career prediction. The rest depends on development, opportunities and careful management.

#1786. Bournemouth’s Adams lauds ‘incredible manager’ Rose

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Tyler Adams lauded Marco Rose as an "incredible manager" as Bournemouth prepare to return from the international break and keep up their sparkling form.

Bournemouth went into the break on the back of a 2-1 win over Ipswich Town, which left them seventh in the Premier League.

Since a 5-1 defeat to Chelsea on October 10, the Cherries have reeled off eight straight wins across all competitions.

Only Arsenal (67), Manchester City (59), and Brighton (50) have collected more Premier League points in 2026 than Bournemouth (49 – W12 D13 L4), with the Cherries aiming to win five successive games in the top flight for the very first time when they take on Nottingham Forest on Saturday.

And though Rose had a slow start to his tenure after he replaced Andoni Iraola, Bournemouth have now hit their groove.

Rose deserves all the credit, so says Adams, who told Bournemouth's media channels: "He's an incredible manager. I'm not just saying that because he’s my manager now. The way that he looks at the game, the way that he breaks it down, I think we're going through a period of evolution, which at times takes a period of adjustment and adaptation.

"But you can see the things that we’re starting to change and the things that are starting to click at the same time.

"With the ball, we have a lot of ideas that we’re trying to execute and get guys into good positions to score goals. Some guys are playing in different positions that they weren’t accustomed to playing last year, and there's a little bit of a different formation as well. But the ideas are starting to click, and he has a lot of good ideas."

Bournemouth are competing in Europe for the first time, and Adams says the squad are learning to cope with a hectic fixture list.

He said: "It's extremely difficult. The most important thing is that you need a full squad of players, guys who are always ready to play and compete.

"When you just have Premier League games and there's one game a week, sometimes the same players play every single week. But balancing that competition, it's nearly impossible. From top to bottom, we need every single player.

"We're in a good place. The morale of the team is good. It's about finding that balance and being able to put in those Thursday, Sunday, Thursday performances over and over again, and repeat it. That's the level of consistency that we have to chase."

While Bournemouth are in fantastic form, Forest beat Manchester City before the international break to move out of the relegation zone.

No player has more goal involvements in the Premier League this season than Evanilson (nine – five goals, four assists), while only Elliot Anderson (30), John McGinn (25), and Boubacar Kamara (24) have won more fouls than his 22.

Delap leads the Premier League this season for both shot-ending carries (14) and goal-ending carries (three), while, among players with over 50% of their minutes played as a central striker this season, only Matheus Cunha (33) has recorded more 10+ metre progressive carries than his 26.

His double propelled Oliver Glasner's team to that much-needed win over Man City on November 7.

Glasner is set to take charge of his 100th Premier League game (W33 D32 L34), though he has yet to beat Bournemouth in the competition (D3 L2), the joint-most he has faced a side without tasting victory.

Bournemouth are first and joint-first, respectively, for shot-ending high turnovers (20) and goal-ending high turnovers (three) in the Premier League this season, while they have had the joint-most shots following opposition errors (18) and scored the most goals from those situations (eight), four more than any other side.

Forest are looking to win successive Premier League games for the second time this calendar year, after a run of three victories in April/May last season. Indeed, in 2026, 60% of their points have come away from home (21/35), the highest proportion in the competition.

However, Forest are winless in their last six away league games against Bournemouth (D2 L4), since a 2-1 victory in the 2014-15 Championship campaign.

#1781. Report: Barcelona set price and now Liverpool deal can move forward

Liverpool can move forward with a transfer after Barcelona named their price for the player. The ball is firmly in the Reds' court now.

Liverpool need a new left-back. That much is abundantly clear to everyone and it’s something that will inevitably happen in 2027 - it’s just a matter of when.

They might move in January, depending on how Andoni Iraola views the current squad. It’s clear he’s not enamoured with either Milos Kerkez or Kostas Tsimikas by the way he’s constantly rotating the pair.

Kerkez, though, is here for the long term. Liverpool invested in him and he’s still so young - there’s zero reason to write him off at this stage and we’re still confident that he’ll make it at Anfield.

However, Tsimikas’s contract expires next summer and we see no real chance that he gets a new one. Liverpool will have to find competition for Kerkez, both to give him a reason to keep pushing and to hedge the bets here.

Liverpool, after all, are far more likely to find an elite left-back if they’re investing in two, rather than going all-in on Kerkez.

Barcelona set Alex Balde priceBarcelona have reportedly set their price for Alejandro Balde. The full-back is wanted by several clubs across Europe, including Juventus. Corriere dello Sport reports on the back of that. They're saying that Barcelona are open to a loan deal, which may suit Juve, but would also sell permanently at €40m and above.

Barcelona have reportedly set their price for Alejandro Balde. The full-back is wanted by several clubs across Europe, including Juventus.

Corriere dello Sport reports on the back of that. They're saying that Barcelona are open to a loan deal, which may suit Juve, but would also sell permanently at €40m and above.

Liverpool are also interested in Balde. The player wasn't keen on leaving Catalonia back in the summer but things have reportedly changed. His agent, Jorge Mendes, has held tentative talks with the Reds, supposedly.

The door is now open, then. A deal with the Reds has room to move forward with Barcelona's price now known and the real question is whether Liverpool actually want to pay that.

It's essentially what they paid for Kerkez and the idea of having two left-backs worth over €40m does seem a bit mad. Especially when so many other areas of the squad require consideration and probably investment.

Balde, though, may be as sure of a thing as Liverpool can get at that price point. One thing's for sure - it'll tempt them.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Keira Walsh is confident Chelsea are in an excellent spot after their "massive" Women's Champions League victory over Paris Saint-Germain.

Veerle Buurman turned home from Lucy Bronze's delivery in the 87th minute at Plough Lane on Wednesday.

Sjoeke Nusken had just seen an effort cleared off the line, with Buurman converting from the resulting corner.

While Chelsea had 17 shots and created chances worth 2.67 expected goals, Sonia Bompastor's team were not at their free-flowing best.

"We spoke about it before the game about wanting to finish the evening on top. We are in a good spot going into the last game."

Chelsea have kept a clean sheet in all five of their Champions League outings this season, and Walsh said: "Whoever plays in the back three, we're really solid. It's something we've concentrated on compared with last season."

#1779. Hutchinson admits ‘dream’ is to be bought by Milan and insists Scudetto is possible

Omari Hutchinson has spoken about his preferred role, while praising the AC Milan fans and revealing his belief the Scudetto is a realistic target.

Hutchinson joined Milan on an initial loan deal from Nottingham Forest with an option to buy. He scored his first goal for the club in the away win over Udinese last month, and is getting more regular minutes on the right side.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In fact, the head coach Ruben Amorim has even deployed him as a wing-back on occasion. Given the injuries to Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze the Englishman’s role has become an even more important one than first imagined.

Hutchinson met with fans this afternoon at the Milan Store in San Babila in the city centre. While at the event, the winger gave an interview to the reporters who were present, with MilanNews relaying his words.

How have these first few months at Milan been? Are you raising your game?

“It’s going well, the coach is happy, but I think there’s still a lot to do. I’m earning myself some space… From here on out, we have to keep winning.”

We often see you on the wing. Do you prefer to play there or as a second striker?

“Personally, I like to play anywhere, but preferably on the right flank. Then, wherever the coach puts me, I try to adapt, do my job, and perform to my best, following his tactical instructions. He knows what I can do with the ball. He simply tells me to create and give my all.”

“He talks to me about what to do with the ball and to do my best.”

Why this difference in performance between Serie A and the Europa League?

“It’s hard to say… There have been games where we haven’t performed well due to silly mistakes, but I think we need to push forward from now on and get back on track for the Europa League. We have the right team to do it. We need to win and be at our best in every game.”

What has struck you most about the fans in Italy these past months?

“Definitely the passion surrounding the club. At the stadium, everyone is behind the team. It’s fantastic, I’ve never experienced anything like it before.”

“We’ve got the players, we have a good squad, and even though we’re still missing some leaders at times, I think we’re building on that. I think the coaches and the coaching staff are guiding us very well. Once everything clicks together perfectly, we’ll do great things.”

Do you still see yourself at Milan in the coming seasons?

“It’s my dream. After this season, I hope to be signed permanently. I see myself playing here for a long time to come.”

What’s the feeling of playing in a historic stadium like San Siro?

“It’s crazy. The fans, even the away fans… It’s a unique feeling. It makes you want to give your all for the fans, create special moments, and win.”

What are the differences between the Premier League and Serie A?

“They’re both tough. When other teams play against Milan, they always want to give their all. They’re always tough matches. Tactically, it’s more defensive here.

“In the Premier League, you probably have more space and the quality is probably a little higher, but Serie A is a tough league. There’s not that big a difference, there’s not that big a gap.”

Is there any team-mate you’ve grown close to?

“No, I have a good relationship with everyone. They’ve all welcomed me very well, and obviously it’s easier with the guys who speak English.”

Do you dream of making the national team?

“I’m trying to focus on my club. I want to perform well for Milan and then we’ll see.”

#1778. When are the 2026-27 Nations League quarter-finals? Dates, fixtures, teams, how they qualified

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 11:54, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 11:57

The 2026-27 UEFA Nations League quarter-finals will take place in March 2027.

The draw for the final eight will take place on November 20, 2026, where it will be decided which teams will face off against each other for a spot in the semi-finals.

Here, Sports Mole runs through all of the details surrounding next year's matches, including dates, fixtures and how each of the eight teams booked a spot in the quarter-finals.

The first legs of the respective last-eight contests will take place between March 25 and March 27, 2027, with the second legs occurring between March 28 and March 30, 2027.

The draw for the quarter-finals of the 2026-27 Nations League will take place at 11am UK time on November 20 at UEFA's headquarters.

Finishing first in the section means that home advantage is gained for the second leg, while the winners of each group will take on a runner-up from another section.

France, Germany, England and Portugal have been the group winners, with Belgium, Netherlands, Spain and Norway qualifying as runners-up in each section.

Portugal are the holders of the Nations League trophy and also the most successful side in the history of the competition, having won it twice (2019 and 2025).

Spain (2023) and France (2021) have also won the tournament.

Germany, England, Belgium, Netherlands and Norway could become first-time winners of the Nations League in 2026-27, with the final set to take place in June 2027.

France finished first in Group A1 to secure a spot in the quarter-finals of the tournament, claiming 13 points from their six matches, boasting a record of four wins, one draw and one defeat.

Belgium were second in Group A2, one point behind the section winners France, having claimed 12 points from their six games, boasting a record of four wins and two defeats from six games.

Germany finished at the top of Group A2 with 11 points from six matches. Incredibly, each of Germany, Netherlands and Greece had 11 points from six games, but Germany finished at the summit on UEFA''s head-to-head goal difference tiebreaker.

Netherlands managed to sneak second spot in Group A2 ahead of Greece on overall goal difference, with Xavi's team finishing with a record of three wins, two draws and one defeat from six matches.

England spectacularly secured first position in Group A3 courtesy of their standout 3-2 success over Spain in Madrid on Sunday night; the Three Lions won five and lost one of their six games to collect 15 points, and they ultimately had a better overall goal difference.

Spain were bumped back down to second spot in Group A3 due to their loss to England; the reverse to the Three Lions proved to be their first defeat in 90 minutes since March 2024.

Portugal finished at the top of Group A4, boasting 15 points from their six matches, in order to comfortably secure a position in the quarter-finals of the tournament.

Norway managed to sneak into second spot in Group A4 ahead of Denmark on the final matchday, recording a 3-2 success over the Danes, which gave them the advance in the head-to-head tiebreaker.

#1777. Opinion: Andoni Iraola forced to sacrifice 95-goal Liverpool star to sign €70m midfielder

Andoni Iraola has tried his best to turn Liverpool's fortunes around at Anfield since his arrival.

Last term, the club were performing well below expectations and ended up finishing fifth in the Premier League.

In a normal season, managing to qualify for the Champions League would be seen as a decent outcome but, after spending £450 million on new players and winning the title just a season before, it was a bad performance.

Their lack of form resulted in Arne Slot being sacked and left Iraola to deal with all of his shortcomings.

Most of the time, things have gone well but, for them to get even better, changes are going to have to take place in the upcoming transfer window.

Liverpool would have to sell Dominik Szoboszlai or Ryan Gravenberch to sign Lamine Camara

Liverpool's midfield has been one of their main problems since 2023.

The July of 2023 was when Fabinho exited Anfield and, since then, the Reds haven't had a natural number six among their ranks.

Alexis Mac Allister, Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch have all been used there to try and plug the gap.

And, while Gravenberch did fairly well during the Reds' title-winning season, from that point on, he's failed to meet expectations.

That's why in the 2026-27 summer transfer window, fans were sure that a new number six would be brought in.

Obviously, Richard Hughes and Iraola didn't feel the need to do that, even though the Spaniard's double pivot has been the thing to cause them the most issues so far.

Several different players were linked as potential options for the Reds to explore but, according to an update from David Lynch via Anfield Index, the Reds would have to sell Gravenberch or Szoboszlai to make room for someone such as Lamine Camara.

"I know the reports, but still struggle to see Lamine Camara to Liverpool in January without a significant departure," he said.

"Endo doesn’t play at all, more a Gravenberch or Szoboszlai which it’s hard to see, otherwise there’s a questions of minutes. Liverpool don’t like to be over stocked as we know."

Liverpool would have to spend around €70m to sign Lamine Camara

Before the 2026-27 season got fully underway, Liverpool were heavily linked with Camara.

In fact, some outlets were even reporting that a deal for the Senegal international was going to be done before the end of the transfer window.

That obviously never ended up happening and now, they're being linked once again with the form of Szoboszlai and Gravenberch raising a fair few questions.

But, for the Reds to sign Camara, it's been reported that a fee worth around €70 million would have to be spent for AS Monaco to even think about letting him go.

Since they rejected his move to Chelsea during the dying embers of the window, he's gone from strength to strength and now, the Ligue 1 outfit are seeing that he's worth a lot of money.

Right now, nothing is decided but, sacrificing someone such as Szoboszlai feels like a big leap, especially for an unproven player in the Premier League.
